pr_title: Allow mods to specify incompatibility types which they implement themselves
pr_body: Closes #13543 (just combined that fix with this change as an example usage). I think there are likely other cases where we can simplify incompatibility specifications remaining.

issue_context.title: Mod "Approach Different" can be used with mods that hide the approach circle
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** 
Approach Different mod could be used with the Hidden mod, which doesn't make much sense

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20320769/122463471-d699ea80-cfdf-11eb-9b06-31c689e7e567.png)

**osu!lazer version:** 
Commit 880a008e01cb78b623e7bea355d29999fbe601a3
comments: Seems pretty straightforward, `OsuModApproachDifferent` should be incompatible with mods that hide the approach circle, such as `ModHidden` as mentioned above, and also `ModSpinIn` and `OsuModObjectScaleTween`.

review_comments: Not too happy about this new param existing,  but `DeselectTypes()` needs to disappear as a method at some point as it's doing a very crude approximation of the mod incompatibility logic anyways, so I'm willing to look away here.

A little unfortunate that implementing the interface is not enough and this spec has to exist, but alas...

Maybe this can be enforced with a test at least? Something like, find all implementors of `IMutateApproachCircles` in this project, and ensure they're all pairwise-incompatible?

To make sure there is symmetry between interface application?

Sounds good, but probably part of a larger test suite to cover all mods, would rather get this change in today with minimal changes (before a release tonight or tomorrow).

> To make sure there is symmetry between interface application?

Yeah that would be the intention. The alternative would be to somehow mark the interface itself as mutually exclusive and handle that in the incompatibility logic but I'm not sure we want more complexity there, which is why I didn't suggest it.

> Sounds good, but probably part of a larger test suite to cover all mods, would rather get this change in today with minimal changes (before a release tonight or tomorrow).

Ok, fair.
